title: Parse-time contract fallback swallows ImportError/RuntimeError that the runtime boundary check was deliberately narrowed to re-raise (silent-failure drift)
description: Both _compute_contract_resolve_fallback_exceptions (line 268: `[ConfigError, OSError, ImportError, RuntimeError]`) and the live predicate _is_contract_resolve_fallback_exception (line 284: `isinstance(exc, (ConfigError, OSError, ImportError, RuntimeError))`) treat ImportError and RuntimeError as recoverable 'fall back to opaque contract' conditions. Their docstrings explicitly claim they mirror the runtime boundary check: line 262-263 says 'Matches ``_execute_lazy._BOUNDARY_CHECK_EXCEPTIONS`` — the parse-time fallback must not swallow more than the runtime boundary check would', and line 281-282 says 'Matches ``_execute_lazy``'. That invariant is now VIOLATED. The runtime sibling (_execute_lazy._compute_boundary_check_exceptions / _is_boundary_check_exception) was deliberately narrowed in commit 34aff403 ('Phase 3 audit — narrow 4 exception catches') from `[ConfigError, OSError, ImportError, RuntimeError]` down to `(ConfigError, OSError, MlflowException)`, with a detailed rationale in its docstring (_execute_lazy.py:140-150): RuntimeError ('Persistently corrupt model artifact' from _load_with_bounded_retry) and ImportError (missing catboost/rustystats backend) are real deploy/infra bugs that must surface loudly, NOT be silently downgraded to an opaque contract. The parse-time copy in _config_builder.py was not updated in that commit (34aff403 touched only _execute_lazy.py), so it still carries the old wide set. Consequence: if a node declares `contract=...` and _derive_parse_time_contract raises ImportError or RuntimeError (e.g. a contract function that imports an optional backend, or a corrupt-artifact RuntimeError), _validate_user_contract (line 334-346) catches it and silently treats the builder as fully opaque (Contract.opaque()), so a genuinely drifted/wrong user contract annotation passes parse-time validation unflagged — exactly the silencing the runtime narrowing was meant to prevent. The referenced symbol `_BOUNDARY_CHECK_EXCEPTIONS` in the docstring does not even exist (the real names are _compute_boundary_check_exceptions / _is_boundary_check_exception), confirming the docstring drifted from reality.
evidence: git show 34aff403 -- src/haute/_execute_lazy.py shows the line `-    exc_types: list[...] = [ConfigError, OSError, ImportError, RuntimeError]` replaced by `+    exc_types: list[...] = [ConfigError, OSError]`, with commit body 'Dropped RuntimeError and ImportError from the tuple. Kept: (ConfigError, OSError, MlflowException)'. `git show 34aff403 --name-only` lists only src/haute/_execute_lazy.py (config_builder untouched). Runtime predicate _execute_lazy.py:171 now reads `if isinstance(exc, (ConfigError, OSError)):` whereas parse-time _config_builder.py:284 still reads `if isinstance(exc, (ConfigError, OSError, ImportError, RuntimeError)):`. The two are no longer in sync despite the docstring asserting they are, and the parse-time set is a strict SUPERSET, so it 'swallows more than the runtime boundary check would' — the exact condition the docstring says must not happen.
